newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB says 1.5-2.0 mln T grain sales to be deferred.
newsitem.headline: CWB says 1.5-2.0 mln T grain sales to be deferred.

text.p: Between 1.5 million and 2.0 million tonnes of Canadian grain sales will be deferred into the next crop year because of rail shipment delays that caused vessel backlogs at Pacific ports and congestion in country elevators, the Canadian Wheat Board said on Tuesday.
"The CWB estimates that 1.5 to 2.0 million tonnes of shipping capacity has been lost and this grain will not move until after August 1, 1997," the CWB said in a statement.
The agency said it will not accept any farmer deliveries of any grades of Canada Western Red Spring wheat in its third quarterly delivery contract.

The CWB also declined to accept any grades of Canada Prairie Spring Red wheat, Canada Prairie Spring White wheat and Canada Western Extra Strong wheat but was accepting all other milling and feed wheat varieties.
No1, No2 and No3 Canada Western Amber Durum wheat will not be accepted but No4 and No5 CWAD will be accepted, CWB said.
All Extra No1 Canada Western barley, No1 and No2 Canada Western barley and Standard Canada Western hulless barley will be accepted, it said.
"Poor railway performance has had a direct impact on the amount of grain the CWB is able to accept," the CWB said.
Heavy snow, extreme cold and equipment failure led to delays in shipping grain by rail to Pacific ports from the Prairies since early January.

As a result, the CWB started railing grain through the United States to U.S. ports in Portland and the Gulf of Mexico after as many as 34 ships were berthed on Canada's west coast March 5. One vessel had waited there as long as 62 days.
On Monday, 26 ships were waiting to load on Canada's Pacific coast with the longest wait being 51 days, CWB said.
"This is causing congestion at country elevators and has limited the amount of grain the CWB can call," it said.

Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said Thursday the Japan Food Agency was concerned about the shipment delays and that the CWB had deferred sales but there was no evidence of lost sales as of March 13.
The CWB said a month ago it faces more than C$15 million in demurrage fines on the number of vessels waiting to load.
Grain not accepted in the third quarterly contract will be automatically considered in the next quarter if farmers chose that option on their 1996/97 contracts, the CWB said.
Farmers who did not choose that option or want to offer more grain have to May 30 to sign the next delivery contract.
Farmers have 14 days to cancel their contracts in cases where Tuesday's CWB acceptance notice on varieties and grades is less than 100 percent.
